card.stem: An extension to a house has a highly insulated flat roof with a waterproof roof covering, as shown.
card.questionText:
Calculate the U-value of the roof, given the construction has the following sequence and data: Waterproof covering thickness 2 mm; roof insulation thickness 150 mm; plywood decking thickness 20 mm; clear cavity between roof joists thickness 200 mm; ceiling insulation thickness 50 mm; plasterboard thickness 12.5 mm.
Thermal data of the flat roof: resistance of external surface (R) 0.048 m² °C/W; resistivity of waterproof covering (r) 6.250 m °C/W; conductivity of roof insulation (k) 0.022 W/m °C; conductivity of plywood (k) 0.130 W/m °C; resistance of clear cavity (R) 0.170 m² °C/W; conductivity of ceiling insulation (k) 0.022 W/m °C; conductivity of plasterboard (k) 0.250 W/m °C; resistance of internal surface (R) 0.122 m² °C/W.

rows.contextNote: Eight resistances, 3 each, by R = T/k (or R = T × r): external surface 0.048 (given); waterproof covering 0.002 × 6.250 = 0.013; roof insulation 0.150/0.022 = 6.818; plywood 0.020/0.130 = 0.154; clear cavity 0.170 (given); ceiling insulation 0.050/0.022 = 2.273; plasterboard 0.0125/0.250 = 0.050; internal surface 0.122 (given). All in m²°C/W.
Total resistance Rt = 9.647 m²°C/W (the sum of all the resistances).
U = 1 ÷ Rt = 1 ÷ 9.647 = 0.104 W/m²°C, with units.

rows.verbatim: Discuss two Passive House design features
rows.contextNote: Any two of the three, each notes 5 and sketches 5 = 10. Foundation design: highly insulated to a U-value of 0.10–0.15 W/m²K; no thermal bridge at the wall-floor junction; aerated concrete blocks at critical junctions; insulation with high compressive strength; an insulated Passive raft-type foundation. Solar shading: prevents overheating by admitting low winter sun and blocking high summer sun; overhangs or deeper eaves; fixed or adjustable brise-soleil, external blinds, awnings and sliding screens; trees and climbing plants. Thermally efficient building envelope: an unbroken line of insulation and airtightness around the whole building, with every element at its optimum performance; a constant, predictable internal temperature; lower energy use, costs and carbon.
